correctness.rationale:
For \(N=8n+1\), the exact factorization formula \(	au(N)=\prod(e_i+1)\) leaves only two cases when \(4
mid	au(N)\): all \(e_i\) even, or one unique exponent \(e_p\equiv1\pmod4\) and all others even. The latter forces \(p\equiv1\pmod8\). A self-contained norm-Euclidean argument in \(\mathbb Z[\sqrt2]\), plus quadratic reciprocity, gives \(p=A^2-8B^2\); scaling proves \(n=T_m-r^2\). The checker verifies the normalization on every \(0\le n\le100000\), but the infinite claim rests on the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The claim settles an explicit published conjecture on the divisor-count function in its full stated domain. Beyond the yes/no resolution, the proof identifies the exact prime-exponent shape behind every failure of divisibility by \(4\) and converts that shape to a quadratic-norm witness, giving a structural mechanism rather than a table check.
